summary: The Bloody Forest, the free tribes of the red woods: a tribal moot, blood-price, the thorn defence and the road between two crowns.

red_woods.name: The Red Woods
red_woods.desc: A hostile woodland that never accepted the Charters.

red_woods_2.name: The Redbark Oath
red_woods_2.desc: All the tribes have sworn on the red oak to stand together.

closed_border.name: The Closed Border
closed_border.desc: The forest roads are blocked and no stranger is welcome.

smugglers.name: Smugglers' Paths
smugglers.desc: Secret paths bring forbidden goods through the forest, at a price.

hired_axes_spirit.name: Hired Axes
hired_axes_spirit.desc: The forest's fighting men hire out to anyone who pays.

forest_ambush_spirit.name: Forest Ambush
forest_ambush_spirit.desc: Hunters who wait for hours and are gone before the range is found.

forest_ambush_2.name: The Red Ambush
forest_ambush_2.desc: A great trap sprung by a signal horn.

old_defiance.name: The Old Defiance
old_defiance.desc: No tax, no charter, no crown and no truce.

forest_truce.name: The Forest Truce
forest_truce.desc: A quiet understanding with the crown, scrawled on a scrap of bark.

woods_closed.name: The Woods Close
woods_closed.desc: The thorn-hedges are drawn closed and the warbands wait inside.

tax_cart_on_the_forest_road.title: A Tax-Cart on the Forest Road
tax_cart_on_the_forest_road.desc: A tax-cart of the crown has strayed onto the forest roads with two guards and a driver who is very sorry. The moot may take it, let it pass or demand a toll for the privilege of crossing the forest.

forest_truce_offer.title: The Forest Asks for a Truce
forest_truce_offer.desc: A chief of the Bloody Forest stands in the antechamber of the Golden Court, hat in hand, asking for a truce. He has brought no gifts, only a promise that the forest will not trouble the roads if the roads do not trouble the forest.

redbark_envoys.title: Envoys from the Red Woods
redbark_envoys.desc: Envoys of the Red Woods have come to the barrows with gifts of fur and amber and a request: that the two peoples leave each other be. The veiled ones listen in silence, and the envoys wait.

options.name: Agree to leave each other be.

the_forest_offers_blades.title: The Forest Offers Its Blades
the_forest_offers_blades.desc: The chiefs of the Bloody Forest offer the crown their blades for the duration of the war. They ask for nothing but the freedom of the woods afterwards, and the court is suspicious of anything so cheap.

focuses.name: The Red Woods
focuses.desc: The Bloody Forest never accepted the Charters. Its tribes take their name from the red-barked trees of the deep woods and from old feuds, and Chieftain Rasvan Redbark leads their moot.

focuses.name: The Tribal Moot
focuses.desc: Every tribe sends its chief to the moot under the great red oak. Decisions are taken by shouting, and recorded by whoever shouts last.

focuses.name: Blood-Feuds Settled
focuses.desc: The chiefs sit down together and settle, by blood-price, the oldest of the feuds. Hands are cut and clasped, and the tribes agree to look elsewhere for their enemies.

focuses.name: The Redbark Oath
focuses.desc: All the tribes swear on the red oak to stand together against any who come in arms. The oath is in the old tongue, and anyone who breaks it is cast out into the thorns.

focuses.name: The Closed Border
focuses.desc: The roads into the forest are blocked with felled oak and thorn-brake. Tax-carts that stray onto them come back empty, if they come back.

focuses.name: Chieftains of the Hollows
focuses.desc: The chieftains of the hollows are given a seat in the moot beside the great chiefs. They bring few warriors, and a great deal of hard-earned knowledge.

focuses.name: One Forest
focuses.desc: The crown calls them bandits, and they call themselves free. For the first time they agree on one thing: the red woods are one forest, and will be defended as one.

focuses.name: The Blood-Price
focuses.desc: A tax-cart has strayed onto the forest roads. The moot must decide what it owes the crown, if anything, for the tolls the crown has never had the courage to claim.

focuses.name: Smugglers' Paths
focuses.desc: Smugglers' paths run through the forest to the lake and the border, known only to the tribes. A man who wants something from the other side of the Wall will find a guide here, for a price.

focuses.name: Furs and Amber
focuses.desc: Red fox, black marten and amber from the northern streams are sold at the edge of the forest, to buyers who come with cash and leave with their eyes open.

focuses.name: Hired Axes
focuses.desc: The forest's fighting men hire out as guards, escorts and axe-bearers to anyone who pays. They stay loyal to the forest, and are sometimes loyal to the employer.

focuses.name: The Forest Market
focuses.desc: A market grows at the forest's heart, with stalls of canvas and rope. No crown's inspectors have ever seen it, and none are expected.

focuses.name: Wealth of the Woods
focuses.desc: Furs, amber, hired axes and smugglers' fees add up to a surprising fortune. The chiefs spend it on forges, and on the sort of things forges make.

focuses.name: The Thorn Defence
focuses.desc: The forest's edge is planted with thorn-hedge, barbed and tangled, a bow-shot deep. Behind it the warbands wait with their bows, unseen.

focuses.name: Forest Ambush
focuses.desc: The tribes teach their young to wait in silence for hours, to loose together, and to be gone before the enemy has found the range.

focuses.name: Bowmen of the Hollows
focuses.desc: The bowmen of the hollows shoot from the ground, from the trees and from the thorn. They fight as hunters do, patiently and without mercy.

focuses.name: Deadfalls and Snares
focuses.desc: Pits, deadfalls and snare-lines are laid across every path into the deep woods. The tribes know where each one is, and the invader does not.

focuses.name: War-Bands
focuses.desc: Warbands of a few hundred muster at the war-oak, each under a chief of its own. They are not disciplined, but they are very fierce.

focuses.name: The Red Ambush
focuses.desc: The tribes combine their ambushes into one great trap, sprung by a signal horn. An army that enters the red woods in column will not leave it that way.

focuses.name: No Road Through
focuses.desc: The forest roads are closed to all comers, with abatis, palisade and a chief at every crossing. It is a poor welcome, and an effective one.

focuses.name: Between the Crowns
focuses.desc: The Bloody Forest lies between the crown of Parim and the doubtful peace of the north. The chiefs know it, and they know that every kingdom wants something from a forest.

focuses.name: A Truce with Parim
focuses.desc: The moot sends a chief to Parim with a white branch and a plain request: leave the forest alone, and the forest will leave Parim alone. The Golden Court is not famous for its sense of humour.

focuses.name: The Old Defiance
focuses.desc: The chiefs renew the old defiance: no tax, no charter, no crown, and no truce. They have said it for seven centuries and have not yet been disproved.

focuses.name: Words with the Veiled
focuses.desc: Envoys of the Red Woods go quietly to their neighbours in the barrows, those who keep their faces covered and their reasons to themselves. They bring gifts, and they ask for nothing but peace.

focuses.name: Outlaws Welcome
focuses.desc: The forest opens its glades to every outlaw, runaway and landless man who can hold a bow. Some of them are good men, and some are not.

focuses.name: Masters of Our Woods
focuses.desc: Whatever the crowns of the Middle Lands may say, the red woods belong to the tribes. They have held them for longer than any king has had a name.

focuses.name: The Woods Close
focuses.desc: The horns sound in the red woods, and the thorn-hedges are drawn closed. The forest was always a closed place, and now it is closed in earnest.

focuses.name: Blood for the Living
focuses.desc: The chiefs put aside their feud with the crown, for a season, and send word that the red woods will bleed with the living. It is not forgiveness. It is arithmetic.

focuses.name: The Hunters' War
focuses.desc: The warbands go out from the forest in small packs, striking at columns, wagons and camps. The enemy cannot find the hunters, and the hunters cannot be made to stop.

focuses.name: Gifts from the South
focuses.desc: A stranger from the south comes to the moot with iron and promises. He asks nothing at once, and the chiefs, who like iron, do not ask him what he will ask later.

focuses.name: The Forest Follows the Heir
focuses.desc: The Heir has returned, and some of the forest chiefs, who have never followed a king, decide to follow him. It is the first time in seven centuries that the red woods have marched under another's banner.

focuses.name: The Forest Endures
focuses.desc: The war is over and the forest opens its roads, a little. The moot meets under the great red oak, and the chiefs count their dead aloud.

focuses.name: The Red Cords
focuses.desc: The Redbark tie their names into cords dyed red with alder bark, and the Veiled tie theirs into grey. The clan mothers send to the downs to ask whether the two kinds of cord were ever one.

focuses.name: One Tongue in Two Woods
focuses.desc: Orran is spoken in two places only, the red woods and the grey downs, and the Redbark mean to ask the cord-mothers for the eldest cord as a gift between kin. They know the answer may be no, and they ask all the same.

focuses.name: River Names Spoken
focuses.desc: The Vale gave Aenoran names to rivers that the Redbark named first, and the war-chiefs have begun to say the old names aloud at the forest edge. Parim will hear of it soon enough, and the chiefs do not much care.

focuses.name: The Moot of Mothers
focuses.desc: The clan mothers of the red woods speak of one moot for both forests and the downs, as there was before any crown, and the war-chiefs listen for once. It would need the grey cords and the giants' stones to agree, and the Veiled to come.
